docs.title: scrapi
docs.text:
Fetch information from multiple sources and analyse it with an LLM.

scrapi collects content from one or more scrapers, runs structured per-result inference, then produces a final summary — all wired together by a single TOML config file.

flowchart LR
    cfg[TOML config] --> orch[Orchestrator]
    orch --> s1[Scraper 1]
    orch --> s2[Scraper N]
    s1 --> si[Search Inference]
    s2 --> si
    si --> sum[Summary Inference]
    sum --> out[PipelineResult]

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
import scrapi

config = scrapi.load_toml_config("config.toml")
orchestrator = scrapi.make_orchestrator(config)
result = orchestrator.run()

print(result.summary.result)

Get started Configuration reference API Reference

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: scrapi is driven by a TOML config file. The three required top-level sections are [llm], [inference], and [[scrapers]]. The [renderer] section is optional.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
[llm]
provider = "openai"

[llm.config]
azure_endpoint = "https://<your-resource>.openai.azure.com/"
model = "gpt-4.1"

[inference.search]
system_prompt = "You are a financial research analyst."
task_prompt = "Extract the key facts and sentiment from this source relevant to the company's situation and outlook."

[inference.summary]
system_prompt = "You are a financial research analyst."
task_prompt = "Based on all sources, summarise the company's current situation and outlook. Cite your sources."

[[scrapers]]
provider = "yahoo"
[scrapers.fetch]
query = "Apple latest company news"
n = 5

[[scrapers]]
provider = "finance"
[scrapers.fetch]
query = ["AAPL"]

[renderer]
provider = "markdown"
output_path = "~/report.md"

docs.text:
yahoofilefinancesqldummy

Searches Yahoo via DDGS and downloads article HTML via Selenium.

Fetch key Type Description query string Search query n int Maximum number of results

Reads local files and converts them to Markdown for LLM consumption. PDFs use PyMuPDF for accurate table/math rendering; all other formats use MarkItDown.

Fetch key Type Description query list[str] File paths or glob patterns (~ is expanded) 
[[scrapers]]

[scrapers.fetch]
query = ["~/documents/report.pdf", "~/documents/*.md"]

Fetches investor-relevant financial data for ticker symbols via yfinance.

Fetch key Type Description query list[str] Ticker symbols, e.g. ["AAPL", "MSFT"]

Executes a SQL query via SQLAlchemy. The connection string is provided under [scrapers.config].

Config key Type Description connection_string string SQLAlchemy connection string; supports ${VAR} placeholders Fetch key Type Description query string SQL query to execute rows_as_results bool Each row becomes a separate result when true; default false 
[[scrapers]]
provider = "sql"
[scrapers.config]
connection_string = "mssql+pymssql://user:${DB_PASSWORD}@host:1433/mydb"
[scrapers.fetch]
query = "SELECT * FROM schema.table"
rows_as_results = false

Returns synthetic results without any network access. Useful for local testing.

Fetch key Type Description query string Query string (embedded in synthetic result text) n int Number of synthetic results

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose ANTHROPIC_API_KEY API key for the anthropic LLM provider AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY API key for the openai LLM provider

Keys can also be set directly in [llm.config] as api_key.

docs.title: Secret injection in connection strings
docs.text:
The sql scraper supports ${VAR} placeholders anywhere in the connection string. Values are resolved from the environment at instantiation time and URL-encoded automatically, so passwords with special characters work without manual escaping:

[scrapers.config]
connection_string = "postgresql://user:${DB_PASSWORD}@host:5432/mydb"

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
scrapi requires Python 3.12+ and uv.

git clone git@github.com:dheimgartner/scrapi.git
cd scrapi
uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Hello world
docs.text:
The fastest way to verify your installation is with the dummy scraper, which returns synthetic results without any network access:

config.toml
[llm]
provider = "anthropic"

[llm.config]
model = "claude-sonnet-4-6"

[inference.search]
system_prompt = "You are a helpful research analyst."
task_prompt = "Summarise the key points from this source."

[inference.summary]
system_prompt = "You are a helpful research analyst."
task_prompt = "Based on all sources, provide a concise final summary."

[[scrapers]]
provider = "dummy"

[scrapers.fetch]
query = "quarterly earnings"
n = 3

import scrapi

config = scrapi.load_toml_config("config.toml")
orchestrator = scrapi.make_orchestrator(config)
result = orchestrator.run()

print(result.summary.result)

docs.title: Working with results
docs.text:
orchestrator.run() returns a PipelineResult that holds both per-source results and the final summary:

# Iterate over source + inference pairs
for pair in result:
    print(pair.search.source)       # source URL / path / ticker
    print(pair.inference.result)    # per-source verdict

# Access the final aggregated summary
print(result.summary.result)
print(result.summary.paragraphs)   # list of key context paragraphs

docs.title: Saving a report
docs.text:
Add a [renderer] section to your config to automatically save a Markdown report at the end of orchestrator.run():

[renderer]
provider = "markdown"
output_path = "~/report.md"

Or render programmatically:

from scrapi.renderer.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

renderer = MarkdownRenderer(output_path="report.md")
renderer.render(result)
renderer.save()

docs.title: Building a config in Python
docs.text:
Instead of a TOML file, you can build the config dict directly:

from scrapi import parse_config, make_orchestrator

config = parse_config({
    "llm": {
        "provider": "anthropic",
        "config": {"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6"},
    },
    "inference": {
        "search": {
            "system_prompt": "You are a financial research analyst.",
            "task_prompt": "Extract the key facts and sentiment from this source.",
        },
        "summary": {
            "system_prompt": "You are a financial research analyst.",
            "task_prompt": "Summarise the company's current situation. Cite your sources.",
        },
    },
    "scrapers": [
        {"provider": "yahoo", "fetch": {"query": "Apple latest news", "n": 5}},
        {"provider": "finance", "fetch": {"query": ["AAPL"]}},
    ],
    "renderer": {"provider": "markdown", "output_path": "~/report.md"},
})

orchestrator = make_orchestrator(config)
result = orchestrator.run()

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
scrapi's public API is small. In most cases you only need the three symbols exported from the top-level package:

import scrapi

# Load and parse a TOML config file
config = scrapi.load_toml_config("config.toml")

# Or build the config dict programmatically
config = scrapi.parse_config({...})

# Create the orchestrator from the parsed config
orchestrator = scrapi.make_orchestrator(config)

# Run the pipeline
result = orchestrator.run()

docs.title: Inference
docs.text:
scrapi runs inference in two stages:

  1. Search inference — analyses each scraped result individually and extracts structured output.
  2. Summary inference — synthesises all per-result analyses into a final cross-source summary.

Both engines inherit from BaseStructuredInference and use LangChain's structured-output API to guarantee a well-typed response.

docs.title: BaseStructuredInference
docs.text:
BaseStructuredInference(
    llm: BaseChatModel, schema: type[BaseModel]
)

Bases: ABC

Shared base for single-shot structured output calls.

Subclasses implement analyse() with domain-specific signatures and call call_structured() to do the actual LLM invocation.

Attributes:

Name Type Description llm

Chat model used to perform the structured invocation.

schema

Pydantic model class describing the expected output shape. Passed to llm.with_structured_output() so the model's response is parsed and validated into an instance of this schema.

docs.title: LLM Providers
docs.text: All LLM backends inherit from BaseLLM. Each subclass initialises a LangChain chat model via _create_llm() and exposes a stateful prompt() method that appends messages to history.

docs.title: BaseLLM

A new LLM endpoint inherits from this class; its single responsibility is to initialize the llm field via create_llm.

history list[BaseMessage]

Running list of messages exchanged so far, in order. Grows with each call to prompt().

docs.title: Orchestrator
docs.text:
The Orchestrator is the top-level runtime object. It wires scrapers and inference engines together and exposes a single run() method.

In normal usage you create it via make_orchestrator rather than constructing it directly.

docs.title: make_orchestrator
docs.text:
make_orchestrator(config: ScrapiConfig) -> Orchestrator

Creates an Orchestrator from a ScrapiConfig.

Instantiates the LLM, both inference objects, and all scrapers from their respective registries, then wires them into the Orchestrator.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default config ScrapiConfig

Configuration containing LLM, inference, and scraper settings.

required

Returns:

Type Description Orchestrator

A fully instantiated Orchestrator.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
run() -> PipelineResult

Fetches search results, analyses each, and aggregates to a final summary.

Iterates over all scrapers, fetches results via each scraper's fetch kwargs, runs per-result inference on each, then runs summary-level inference over all collected results.

docs.title: Scrapers
docs.text: All scrapers inherit from BaseScraper. Concrete implementations add a _fetch_content() method and a convert_to_ai_content() static method.

docs.title: BaseScraper
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for content scrapers.

All scraper implementations must provide a mechanism for retrieving content from a data source and converting it into a collection of BaseSearchResult objects.

Implementations may obtain their content from search engines, web pages, APIs, document repositories, or other external systems, but should expose a consistent interface through fetch_content().

docs.text:

Wraps _fetch_content and raises if the result is empty or if the underlying implementation raises any exception.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseScraper

Read local files and convert them to Markdown for LLM consumption.

Each entry in query may be a literal path or a glob pattern; ~ is expanded. PDF files are processed via PyMuPDF for faithful table and math rendering; all other formats are handled by MarkItDown.

SQLScraper(connection_string: str)

Bases: BaseScraper

Execute SQL queries and return result sets via SQLAlchemy.

Each instance is bound to a single database via connection_string. Passwords (or other secrets) can be injected using ${ENV_VAR} placeholders in the connection string, e.g.::

postgresql://user:${DB_PASSWORD}@host/db

The placeholder is resolved from the environment at instantiation time.
